events.name: Route 25: The Horde
events.intro: A horde of Angry Mankey spills onto the road and will not let you pass. Five of them, one after another.

success.text: The first three rush you together.

events.name: Route 25: A Breather
events.intro: Three down. The last two Mankey are working themselves into a rage behind the rocks.

success.text: You get a minute to patch everyone up.
No time to lose.

events.name: Route 25: The Fourth
events.intro: The fourth Mankey screams and charges.

success.text: It goes down, and the last one steps out.

events.name: Route 25: Mankey's Wrath
events.intro: The fifth is no Mankey. A Primeape, wild with rage, uses Rage again and again.

choices.label: Calm the Primeape down the hard way

success.text: The horde falls quiet. One Mankey steps out of the grass and sets its jaw: it wants to come with you.

events.name: Saffron Fighting Tournament
events.intro: A banner over the dojo yard: THE SAFFRON FIGHTING TOURNAMENT. Thirty-two fighters, Fighting types only, one Pokémon each. The organizer eyes your Mankey.

success.text: The sign-up sheet has thirty-two names. Yours goes at the bottom. Only your fighter steps onto the mat.
The sign-up sheet has thirty-two names. Yours goes at the bottom. Only your fighter steps onto the mat.
You leave it for the next trainer.

events.name: Tournament: Round of 32
events.intro: Round of 32. One Pokémon each, matched to yours. If yours faints, you are out.

success.text: Round of 32: a fighter your size.

events.name: Tournament: Round of 16
events.intro: Round of 16. One Pokémon each, matched to yours. If yours faints, you are out.

success.text: Round of 16: a fighter your size.

events.name: Tournament: Quarterfinal
events.intro: Quarterfinal. One Pokémon each, matched to yours. If yours faints, you are out.

success.text: Quarterfinal: a fighter your size.

events.name: Tournament: Semifinal
events.intro: Semifinal. One Pokémon each, matched to yours. If yours faints, you are out.

success.text: Semifinal: a fighter your size.

events.name: Tournament: The Final
events.intro: The final. Across the mat stands the rival Mankey: the same kind as yours, the same level, and it wants the belt as much as you do.

success.text: The crowd chants for both of you.

events.name: Saffron Fighting Dojo
events.intro: The Fighting Dojo next door is open. Its master, arms folded, offers a one-on-one: his Machamp against your whole team.

success.text: The master bows. Machamp cracks its knuckles.
You bow and leave the dojo.

events.name: Dojo: The Master’s Gift
events.intro: The master nods. "You earned a student. Choose."

success.text: Hitmonlee bows and falls in step beside you.
Hitmonchan bows and falls in step beside you.

events.name: Dojo: The Master’s Gift
events.intro: The master nods, then calls a third student out of the back. "Today I can offer three. Choose."

success.text: Hitmonlee bows and falls in step beside you.
Hitmonchan bows and falls in step beside you.
Hitmontop bows and falls in step beside you.

events.name: The Copycat Girl
events.intro: A girl in a bow follows you down the street, repeating every word you say and every step you take. She holds out a hand: "Copy me! Four claps!"

success.text: You match all four. She squeals, copies your Pokémon’s cry note for note, and hands you a TM: Mimic.

failure.text: You miss a clap. She copies your embarrassed face, giggles, and skips away.

success.text: She copies your wave and your walk, all the way out of town.

events.name: Silph Co.: The Lobby
events.intro: The lobby of the Silph Co. tower: marble floors, a hushed receptionist, a single elevator. The president himself comes down to meet visitors.

success.text: He thanks you for keeping the city safe and hands you a Poké Ball: a Lapras, bred for ferrying people across the water. "Something is wrong upstairs," he adds quietly. The building stays open to you.
Word has gone round that you are being hunted. The guards cross their arms. The lobby is as far as you get.

events.name: Saffron Magnet Train
events.intro: The Magnet Train hums in its station, bound for the coast. A ride would carry you most of the way across, but you would see nothing of the road.

success.text: The city blurs. You step off right beside the Gym, with nothing found along the way.
You watch it glide away without you.

events.name: Sabrina's Labyrinth
events.intro: A fortune-teller in a violet shawl stops you outside the Gym, and her hands are cold when she takes yours. "Let me read your aura." A town guide hurries over, whispering about a special entrance that few ever see, one the Gym keeps behind a painted wall. Both of them are smiling a little too long. Somewhere behind the plaster, something that is not wind is breathing out.

success.text: Your Poké Balls rattle against your belt, then go quiet, one by one, like children told to hush. The world tilts, and you are not holding your own weight anymore.
Your Poké Balls rattle against your belt, then go quiet, one by one, like children told to hush. The world tilts, and you are not holding your own weight anymore.
You decline. Nothing changes.

events.name: The Ghost Returns
events.intro: The screen goes black. Silence. Then a face lunges out of the dark, all teeth and eyes, and holds there. It wavers, and the fright melts into something shy. It asks, very quietly, to join your team.

success.text: It has not forgotten the Labyrinth, or you.
It fades, and the dark lets go of the screen.

events.name: Labyrinth: The First Fight
events.intro: You are standing in a corridor of violet stone, and your Pokémon are not with you. They are scattered through the Labyrinth, each shut in a shadow lantern like a candle behind glass; you can feel them the way you feel a missing tooth. A hooded shape fills the passage ahead. You reach for a Poké Ball and your hand closes on nothing, and then you look down at the hand and see the floor through it. This fight was lost before it began, and you know it, and the thing in the hood knows it too. A tombstone pushes up through the floor with your own name half carved on it. Then the dark above you fills with wings that are not wings: a swarm of Ghost-types, hundreds of them, pours across the whole sky of the room, laughing without sound. When it has passed, one small ghost is left hovering at the height of your knee. It will not look straight at you. "I can help you get your body back," it says. "I know the way. Nobody ever asks me to."

success.text: You swing at it with a fist that is only an idea. It does not even step back. The small ghost tugs your sleeve, gently: not that way. You let it lead you around the shape, and the shape lets you go, as if you were already something it had finished with.

choices.label: Back away and follow the ghost

success.text: You back down the corridor until the wall is there. The small ghost presses close, and it is warmer than you expected a ghost to be. "Walk where I walk," it whispers. "Put your feet where mine are not."

events.name: Labyrinth: The Body in the Next Room
events.intro: Room 1 of 6. Through a doorway you have not entered, you see yourself. Your own body stands in the middle of a room with its back to you, perfectly still, one hand a little raised as if it had been interrupted in the middle of reaching for something. The door will not let you in; each time you lean toward it the frame is a little narrower. The small ghost lifts the same hand you are lifting. You didn't notice at first. When you tilt your head, it tilts its head. It is copying you, shyly and exactly, the way a child copies the one grown-up who was kind to it. In the corner of the room, one lantern glows, and inside it something small is pressed against the glass.

choices.label: Call out to your own body

success.text: Your voice leaves you as a breath of cold mist, and the body in the room does not turn. But the lantern's glow shifts toward you, and the ghost says, very quietly, "It heard. It just can't answer yet." It slips through the wall, comes back with the lantern, and a Pokémon you know steps out of the light and fades in beside you as a pale shape, wagging, delighted, afraid.

choices.label: Hold still and watch your body

success.text: You make yourself stand as still as the thing in the room, and the ghost, copying, goes still too, and for a long moment two of you are listening. You see the body's raised hand tremble. It is trying, from very far away, to reach back. The lantern cracks open on its own, as if in answer.

The frame narrows and narrows until your arm is stuck to the elbow in the wall. The ghost pulls on your other arm with all it has. When you come free, you are holding the lantern instead of the door. It was never the door that mattered.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Ghosts of Your Party
events.intro: Room 2 of 6. The hallway bends, and at the bend, in the glass of a window that has no outside, you see them: your Pokémon, as ghosts. Pale, half-finished, each one turning its head toward you in the way you taught it to. They are not dead. You can tell, because they are still doing the small habits you know: one scratching its ear, one standing a step in front of the others. The sight hurts anyway, like looking at a photograph of a person who is in the next room. Then the shapes in the glass turn their heads the wrong way, all together, and the hall is full of Possessed shades with your Pokémon's faces held up in front of them like masks. The small ghost has stopped copying you. It has moved one step ahead of you, a little, and does not seem to know it did.

success.text: The ghost fights alone, because it is all you have, and it is smaller than anything it faces.

events.name: Labyrinth: Doors From Somewhere Else
events.intro: Room 3 of 6. A corridor of doors, one after another, and none of them belongs in a gym. One is salt-stained and has the sound of the sea behind it: a harbour you walked through two regions ago. One is a train-station door with a bell that is still ringing. One is the oak front door of the first town you ever left, with a cracked doorstep you would know blind. Every door is slightly open. You can smell each place, and it smells exactly as you left it, down to the cooking. The ghost goes to the third door, then stops, looking back at you, and for the first time it asks a question instead of copying: "Which one do you want to go home through?"

success.text: Cold spray touches your face, and gulls cry far off, and a pale light falls across the floor from the tide that is not there. You step through and the hallway comes with you, but you are carrying the smell of salt, and the lantern ahead is brighter for it.

The bell rings once more as you pass. You catch an announcement in a voice you half know, calling a train that has already left, and you stand a moment longer than you should have. The lantern flares as if it had been waiting for a reason to.

choices.label: The door of your first town

success.text: You do not go through it. You put your palm on the wood and feel, on the other side, someone's palm. The ghost leans against your leg. "You can come back," it says, "when it is over." Then the door closes softly and a lantern drops out of the dark into your hands.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Villager Who Says One Thing
events.intro: Room 4 of 6. In the middle of a room full of folded tablecloths and plates laid for no one, a villager stands facing the wall. He says the same sentence, and says it again, in exactly the same voice, as though a needle had stuck in the groove of him: "You are late for dinner. You are late for dinner. You are late for dinner." He is not frightening. That is the worst of it. He turns when you come near, and his eyes are wet and polite, and he says it again, with the small hope of a man hoping this time it will be the right answer. The ghost is no longer copying you at all. It floats forward, past you, and looks at the man the way you would look at someone you recognise.

choices.label: Tell him you're sorry for being late

success.text: "I'm sorry," you say, and mean it, to a man you have never met. His shoulders let go. He says, once, a different sentence: "Thank you. We kept it warm." The lantern on the table beside the plates opens.

"You are late for dinner," you say, softly, and his face breaks open, because someone finally said it with him. He sits at the table and begins to eat the nothing on the plate, and for a while it is the happiest thing you have ever seen. The lantern opens.

He opens his mouth and the sentence does not come. A long breath. Then, in a small, plain voice: "My daughter. She did not want to come in to dinner without me." Your throat closes. The ghost takes the lantern from the table with great tenderness and gives it to you without a word.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Drawings
events.intro: Room 5 of 6. The walls here are covered edge to edge in children's drawings, in crayon, in pencil, in what looks like jam. Every one of them is of you and your team. Some are good, with all the right colours. Some are wrong in ways that sit in your chest: a smile where there should not be one, a Pokémon with too many eyes, a tiny stick figure with its mouth drawn as a straight line, labelled in careful letters, MY FRIEND WHO IS LOST. The ghost stops in front of one drawing and does not move. In it, there is a small ghost, and a trainer holding its hand, and the sun is a huge yellow circle with a face. It is the only drawing in the room where everyone is smiling. The ghost goes first, now. It does not look back to see whether you are following.

choices.label: Take the drawing of your party

success.text: You peel it off the wall carefully, as if it could bruise. Every Pokémon on it is drawn at the right height, with the right ears. Someone watched you very closely to draw this. The lantern behind it opens, and the ghost leads you out of the room with the drawing held to your chest.

choices.label: Take the drawing with the ghost in it

success.text: The ghost sees what you have taken and flushes with a violet glow that is almost a blush. It does not say thank you. It floats ahead of you and does not turn, but it moves slower, so that you can walk beside it.

choices.label: Leave them all where they are

success.text: You leave every drawing on its wall, because they are hers, or his, or theirs, and not yours to take. A pencil on the floor rolls toward you. You pick it up and, on an empty bit of wall, you draw one small sun with a face. The lantern behind the wall opens by itself.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Small Grave
events.intro: Room 6 of 6. A last small room, and in the middle of it, a grave no larger than a loaf of bread. A stone with a Pokémon's name on it, and it is the name of a Pokémon you have never lost. You stand and read it twice. It is a Pokémon that is still alive, still waiting in a lantern somewhere, still counting on you. Someone here has already decided that you will fail. Flowers have been laid on the grave, and they are fresh. The ghost settles beside the stone. For a while it says nothing at all. Then: "I used to have a grave like this one. I don't remember whose." It has led you all the way here without once looking at the way, and it knows the last door. It looks at you, and for the first time it does not wait for you to go first.

success.text: You say the name aloud, clearly, and the stone shivers, and the flowers wilt in a single breath. That is not your Pokémon's name any longer: that is only a name, and your Pokémon is somewhere behind the next wall, calling for you. The last lantern opens, and your whole team is here at last, a ring of pale shapes, and the ghost at the front of them.

choices.label: Kneel by the grave with the ghost

success.text: You kneel, and the ghost settles against your side, and the two of you stay like that for a time that has no length. It does not tell you whose grave it is. You do not ask. When you stand, the stone has crumbled to a handful of grey dust, and the lantern behind it is open.

You tear the small stone out of the floor and throw it against the wall, and it breaks with a sound like a child's cry. The ghost flinches, and then, slowly, it forgives you. Behind the broken stone: the last lantern, and every one of your Pokémon waiting to follow.

events.name: Labyrinth: Sabrina's Alakazam
events.intro: The last door opens onto a gym that is entirely mirror and violet light, and at the heart of it Sabrina sits with her Alakazam, who is not looking at you, because it does not need to. "You are only a ghost," she says, kindly, the way you speak to a child who will wake up tomorrow and forget. "Go back to sleep." You can feel your body, finally, across the room: a still shape at her feet, breathing slowly, held in place by a hundred small psychic threads. The ghost floats forward and stops between you and her. "I will stand in front of you," it says, and its voice shakes. "I have never stood in front of anyone before." This is a fight you cannot command as you are used to. Every turn, one of your four moves is a lie: it shows one move, and does another. Every second turn the ghost can see true, and will mark the false one for you.

success.text: The ghost faces her, and you stand behind it, and you do not look away.
